reason: S1 adds an externally reachable LZIP decoder implementing base.io_transformer, while H0 compiles only AUX__JSON, BASE, and JSON modules and invokes only wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson. Consequently, no input reaches the new decoder or exercises its transformer lifecycle, suspension handling, closed-source truncation behavior, destination backpressure, one-byte work-buffer contract, or QUIRK_IGNORE_CHECKSUM state.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON but no LZIP, LZMA, or CRC32 module.
H0's production entry points are wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens in fuzz_complex/fuzz_simple and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson in fuzz_cpp; it never constructs a lzip.decoder or calls transform_io.
S1 declares decoder? implements base.io_transformer and exposes decoder.transform_io?, creating a distinct fuzz-worthy API surface.
decoder.transform_io? converts base."$short read" on a closed source into "#truncated input" and otherwise yields status, exposing incremental I/O state and suspension semantics absent from H0.
decoder.set_quirk! accepts base.QUIRK_IGNORE_CHECKSUM, decoder.get_quirk reports it, and unsupported keys return base."#unsupported option"; H0's set_quirks targets only wuffs_json__decoder.

decoder.workbuf_len returns an exact length of DECODER_WORKBUF_LEN_MAX_INCL_WORST_CASE (1), and do_transform_io? writes to dst via write_u8?, introducing work-buffer and short-write behavior not exercised by the token-buffer JSON harness.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated LZIP io_transformer fuzz path that initializes decoder, varies QUIRK_IGNORE_CHECKSUM and unsupported quirk keys, supplies the exact and invalid work-buffer sizes around 1 byte, incrementally limits and closes src, limits/compacts dst to force short writes, repeatedly resumes transform_io until terminal status, and checks progress, bounds, truncation mapping, and quirk round-tripping.
